b.40b3da886f:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
b.869c7a0f72:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Isaía Prophéta
<r>Isa 11:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Et egrediétur virga de radíce Iesse, et flos de radíce eius ascéndet.
<n>2</n> Et requiéscet super eum Spíritus Dómini: spíritus sapiéntiæ et intelléctus, spíritus consílii et fortitúdinis, spíritus sciéntiæ et pietátis;
<n>3</n> Et replébit eum spíritus timóris Dómini: non secúndum visiónem oculórum iudicábit, neque secúndum audítum áurium árguet:
<n>4</n> Sed iudicábit in iustítia páuperes, et árguet in æquitáte pro mansuétis terræ:
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Ecce virgo concípiet, et páriet fílium, dicit Dóminus: et vocábitur nomen eius
* Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.
<r>℣.</r> Super sólium David, et super regnum eius sedébit in ætérnum.
<r>℟.</r> Et vocábitur nomen eius Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.
<r>℟.</r> Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.
b.bb503b7614:

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Isaias
<r>Isa 11:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> And there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root.
<n>2</n> And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom, and of understanding, the spirit of counsel, and of fortitude, the spirit of knowledge, and of godliness.
<n>3</n> And he shall be filled with the spirit of the fear of the Lord. He shall not judge according to the sight of the eyes, nor reprove according to the hearing of the ears.
<n>4</n> But he shall judge the poor with justice, and shall reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Behold, the Virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, saith the Lord;and His name shall be called Wonderful, the Mighty God.
<r>℣.</r> He shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom for ever.
<r>℟.</r> And His name shall be called Wonderful, the Mighty God.
* And His name shall be called Wonderful, the Mighty God.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Isa 11:4-7</r>
<n>4</n> Et percútiet terram virga oris sui, et spíritu labiórum suórum interfíciet ímpium.
<n>5</n> Et erit iustítia cíngulum lumbórum eius: et fides cinctórium renum eius.
<n>6</n> Habitábit lupus cum agno, et pardus cum hædo accubábit, vitúlus et leo et ovis simul morabúntur, et puer párvulus minábit eos.
<n>7</n> Vítulus et ursus pascéntur, simul requiéscent cátuli eórum, et leo quasi bos cómedet páleas.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Obsecro, Dómine, mitte quem missúrus es: vide afflictiónem pópuli tui: Sicut locútus es:
* Veni, et líbera nos.
<r>℣.</r> Qui regis Israël, inténde, qui dedúcis velut ovem Ioseph, qui sedes super Chérubim.
<r>℟.</r> Veni, et líbera nos.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>Isa 11:4-7</r>
<n>4</n> And he shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked.
<n>5</n> And justice shall be the girdle of his loins: and faith the girdle of his reins.
<n>6</n> The wolf shall dwell with the lamb: and the leopard shall lie down with the kid: the calf and the lion, and the sheep shall abide together, and a little child shall lead them.
<n>7</n> The calf and the bear shall feed: their young ones shall rest together: and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> O my Lord, send I pray thee, Him Whom Thou wilt send; see the affliction of thy people. As Thou hast promised, come;And deliver us.
<r>℣.</r> Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, Thou That leadest Joseph like a flock, Thou That sittest upon the Cherubim!
* And deliver us.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<r>Isa 11:8-10</r>
<n>8</n> Et delectábitur infans ab úbere super forámine áspidis, et in cavérna réguli, qui ablactátus fúerit, manum suam mittet.
<n>9</n> Non nocébunt, et non occídent in univérso monte sancto meo: quia repléta est terra sciéntia Dómini, sicut aquæ maris operiéntes.
<n>10</n> In die illa radix Iesse, qui stat in signum populórum, ipsum gentes deprecabúntur, et erit sepúlcrum eius gloriósum.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Ecce dies véniunt, dicit Dóminus, † et suscitábo David germen iustum: † et regnábit rex, et sápiens erit, et fáciet iudícium et iustítiam in terra:
* Et hoc est nomen quod vocábunt eum: † Dóminus iustus noster.
<r>℣.</r> In diébus illis salvábitur Iuda, et Israël habitábit confidénter.
<r>℟.</r> Et hoc est nomen quod vocábunt eum: † Dóminus iustus noster.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Dóminus iustus noster.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<r>Isa 11:8-10</r>
<n>8</n> And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp: and the weaned child shall thrust his hand into the den of the basilisk.
<n>9</n> They shall not hurt, nor shall they kill in all my holy mountain, for the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the covering waters of the sea.
<n>10</n> In that day the root of Jesse, who standeth for an ensign of the people, him the Gentiles shall beseech, and his sepulchre shall be glorious.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch; and a King shall reign in wisdom and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth:
* And this is His name whereby He shall be called: The Lord our Righteous one.
<r>℣.</r> In His days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely.
<r>℟.</r> And this is His name whereby He shall be called: The Lord our Righteous one.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> The Lord our Righteous one.
b.7252907722:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>E</c>xcita, quǽsumus, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut ab imminéntibus peccatórum nostrórum perículis, te mereámur protegénte éripi, te liberánte salvári:
<h>Q</h>ui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.1bcf7c2300:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>S</c>tir up, O Lord, we pray thee, thy strength, and come among us, that whereas through our sins and wickedness we do justly apprehend thy wrathful judgments hanging over us, thy bountiful grace and mercy may speedily help and deliver us;
<h>W</h>ho livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>O</c>ctávo Idus Decémbris Luna vicésima sexta. Anno Dómini 2026
<h>M</h>yræ, quæ est metrópolis Lýciæ, natális sancti Nicolái, Epíscopi et Confessóris, de quo, inter plura miraculórum insígnia, illud memorábile fertur, quod Imperatórem Constantínum ab intéritu quorúmdam se invocántium, longe constitútus, ad misericórdiam per visum mónitis defléxit et minis.
<h>E</h>ódem die sancti Polychrónii Presbýteri, qui, témpore Constántii Imperatóris, cum ad altáre Missas ágeret, invásus est ab Ariánis et iugulátus.
<h>I</h>n Africa sancti Maiórici, fílii sanctæ Dionýsiæ, qui, cum esset adolescéntulus ac torménta pavésceret, matris obtútibus verbísque corroborátus est, et, céteris fórtior factus, in torméntis ánimam réddidit; quem amplexáta mater domi sepelívit, et ad eius sepúlcrum assídue orare consuévit.
<h>I</h>bídem sanctárum mulíerum Dionýsiæ, quæ sancti Maiórici Mártyris éxstitit mater, Datívæ ac Leóntiæ; itémque religiósi viri, nómine Tértii, Æmiliáni médici, et Bonifátii, cum áliis tribus. Hi omnes, in persecutióne Wandálica, sub Ariáno Rege Hunneríco, gravíssimis et innúmeris supplíciis pro cathólicæ fídei defensióne cruciáti, sanctórum Christi Confessórum número sociári meruérunt.
<h>R</h>omæ sanctæ Aséllæ Vírginis, quæ (ut beátus Hierónymus scribit), ex útero matris benedícta, vitam in ieiúniis et oratiónibus usque ad senéctam prodúxit.
<h>G</h>ranátæ, in Hispánia, pássio beáti Petri Paschásii, Epíscopi Giennénsis et Mártyris, ex Ordine beátæ Maríæ de Mercéde redemptiónis captivórum.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.b818fd9dcf:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 6th 2026, the 26th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

<h>A</h>t Myra, which is the chief city of Lycia, (in the year 324,) the holy Confessor Nicolas, Bishop (of that see,) of whom among many other signs and wonders it is recorded that when the Emperor Constantine had condemned certain persons to death and these called upon Nicolas, who was alive, and afar off, he appeared unto the Emperor, and bent him to mercy by exhortation and threats.
<h>O</h>n the same day, the holy priest Polychronius, who was saying Mass in the time of the Emperor Constantius, when the Arians attacked him and slew him, (fourth century.)
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyr Majoricus, the son of holy Dionysia. He was but a little lad and was in fear of the torments, but by the looks and words of his mother, he was so strengthened that he became mightier than them all, and died under the torture his mother took his body to her heart, and buried it in their home, and was used to pray instantly at his grave.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy women Dionysia, Dativa, and Leontia, and the monk Tertius, the physician Aemilian, Boniface, and three others, who in the Vandal persecution under the Arian King Hunneric were tormented in most grievous and manifold ways for their defence of the Catholic faith, and so earned a place among Confessors of Christ, (in the year 484.)
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy Virgin Asella, who, as writeth blessed Jerome, was blessed from her mother's womb, and passed her life in fastings and prayers unto a good old age. (Born about 334 and died about 410.)
<h>A</h>t Granada, in Spain, the blessed martyr Peter Paschasius, Bishop of Jaen, of the order of blessed Mary of Ransom for the redemption of captives, (in the year 1300.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>E</c>xcita, Dómine, corda nostra ad præparándas Unigéniti tui vias: ut, per eius advéntum, purificátis tibi méntibus servíre mereámur:
<h>Q</h>ui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.a053347a53:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>S</c>tir up our hearts, O Lord, to make ready the ways of thine Only-begotten Son, that by His coming our minds being purified, we may the more worthily give up ourselves to thy service:
<h>W</h>ho with thee liveth and reigneth, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.0fcc82d90e:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>E</c>xcita, quǽsumus, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut ab imminéntibus peccatórum nostrórum perículis, te mereámur protegénte éripi, te liberánte salvári:
<h>Q</h>ui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.fa7949a4c6:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>S</c>tir up, O Lord, we pray thee, thy strength, and come among us, that whereas through our sins and wickedness we do justly apprehend thy wrathful judgments hanging over us, thy bountiful grace and mercy may speedily help and deliver us;
<h>W</h>ho livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.274e44e365:
<h>Regula vel Evangelium</h>
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
Reguláribus disciplínis instruat nos Magíster caléstis.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>D</c>onet Dóminus ut observétis hæc ómnia, tamquam spirituális pulchritúdinis amatóres; et bono Christi odóre de bona vestra conversatióne fragrántes: non sicut servi sub lege, sed sicut líberi sub grátia constitúti.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
Commemorátio Fratrum, Sorórum, Familiárium, Benefactórum defunctórum Ordinis nostri.
Requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Psalmus 116</r>
§11.66d6af014b
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Osténde nobis, Dómine, misericórdiam tuam.
<r>℟.</r> Et salutáre tuum da nobis.

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>A</c>ctiónes nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, aspirándo prǽveni et adiuvándo proséquere: ut cuncta nostra orátio et operátio a te semper incípiat, et per te cœpta finiátur.
Per Christum Dóminum nostrum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Adiutórium nostrum ✠ in nómine Dómini.
<r>℟.</r> Qui fecit cælum et terram.
<n>Si non sequitur aliqua Hora dicitur</n>
<r>℣.</r> Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.71da482b7a:
<h>Regula vel Evangelium</h>
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
May the heavenly Master instruct us in the discipline of the Rule.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>M</c>ay the Lord grant that you observe all these things as lovers of spiritual beauty, and giving forth the good odour of Christ by your good life: not as servants under the law, but as free men established under grace.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
Commemoration of the deceased Brethren, Sisters, Relations and Benefactors of our Order.
Requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Psalm 116</r>
§11.0a67a14e81
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Show us, O Lord, thy mercy.
<r>℟.</r> And grant us thy salvation.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>D</c>irect, we beseech thee, O Lord, our actions by thy holy inspiration, and carry them on by thy gracious assistance: that every prayer and work of ours may always begin from thee, and by thee be happily ended.
Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Our help is ✠ in the name of the Lord,
<r>℟.</r> Who made heaven and earth.
<n>Si non sequitur aliqua Hora dicitur</n>
<r>℣.</r> May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
